thread:
Lia: paging oncall — we started seeing a spike in 500s for /v2/prompt-route around 07:11UTC, looks correlated with canary rollout of router-v2-experimental (5%)
Matt: ack, i'm looking. Grafana alert fired: 500-rate > 2% for canary cluster (p95 latency up as well)
oncall-bot: @oncall Dylan, you have been paged for incident INC-2026 (sev2) — /v2/prompt-route elevated errors
deploy-bot: Canary deployment router-v2-experimental -> shard-3 promoted at 07:08UTC by matt.deploy (5% traffic target)
Dylan: on it. can anyone share nginx logs from shard-3?
Jen: past minute logs show upstream reset + KERNEL_CONN_REFUSED 3x from shard-3: router-v2-experimental. rolling errors started ~07:10
Lia: customer impact: internal synthetic checks + small subset of end users (EU region) experiencing errors and latency spikes. No big customers flagged yet but some product teams reporting errors in QA.
Sam: i'm going to hit the kill switch for the experimental FF. Lia, can you confirm the flag key?
Lia: key is `ff.router_prompt_v2_experimental`
Sam: executing: `ffctl toggle ff.router_prompt_v2_experimental --state=off --reason="canary 5% elevated 500s"`
deploy-bot: ffctl: feature flag ff.router_prompt_v2_experimental successfully toggled OFF by sam @ 07:15:12UTC
Matt: i see traffic falling off shard-3, error rate dropping on canary cluster. good.
Dylan: can we confirm global fallback behavior? requests should route to router-v2-stable.
Jen: verified in logs — after toggle, traffic routed to stable, 502s/500s back to baseline within ~40s.
Lia: status update to execs: canary introduced regressions, kill-switch turned on, rollback confirmed. Impact limited to ~2k requests over 7 minutes, no SLA breach expected.
Sam: starting postmortem stub. tagging owners: matt (deploy), jen (runtime), lia (customer comms).
Matt: root cause hypothesis: a change in header propagation in new router caused backends to reject long-lived streaming connections (connection reset pattern). also kernel conn refused points to ephemeral port exhaustion on canary hosts — need to check connection pooling.
Dylan: opening an infra ticket to check netstack config on shard-3 and to validate kernel params (somaxconn, tcp_tw_reuse).
oncall-bot: @channel Incident INC-2026 mitigation: FF killed, traffic rolled back, monitoring will remain for 30m. On-call: Dylan -> handoff to SRE on next shift in 1h.
Lia: product comms — i'll post brief note in #customer-success and ping major accounts. Draft: "We detected errors in an experimental routing feature and temporarily disabled it; routing reverted to stable. No action required on your end. We're investigating and will follow up."
Sam: quick follow-up actions: 1) collect full request traces for the window 07:08-07:16 2) gather network/socket metrics from canary hosts 3) run small controlled canary in staging with increased tcp backlog to reproduce 4) add pre-rollout health check for ephemeral port exhaustion
Matt: for the postmortem we should also capture the decision timeline: deploy -> alert -> page -> kill-ff -> verification. I'll capture timestamps.
Jen: note: we did not have an automated preflight for stream header length; adding a gating test in CI will help.
Dylan: i'm going to keep monitoring for 15m then handoff. If error rate creeps >1% again we'll re-escalate.
Lia: thanks everyone. tagging @product to avoid re-enabling the FF until we have a patch and a new canary plan. :eyes:
Sam: one more — add an automated rollback playbook entry to incident runbook for feature-flag kill scenarios (steps + who toggles + verification commands).
Matt: agreed. I'll include the `ffctl` rollback commands and the log grep snippets in the runbook PR.
Dylan: handing off to SRE team in 20m. leave monitoring alerts unchanged.
Lia: logging done, saving thread to incidents channel, adding follow-up tasks in JIRA INC-2026.
Jen: small note — some of the failed requests were from internal health checks; we should isolate synthetic traffic in metrics to avoid noisy alerts.
Sam: closing loop: ff toggle -> stable routing verified -> no customer escalations. setting severity to P2 post-triage.
Dylan: closing watch in 18m if metrics stable. thx all.
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread for an incident involving feature flag kill-switch on prompt routing experimental canary. All fields are strings or list of strings.
